sections.text:
On a hot summer afternoon, a young, agile deer headed to a spring of mirror-clear water to quench its thirst.

After he drank and quenched his thirst, he stood still, looking at his reflection in the calm water.

The deer was very impressed by the shape of its long, forked and branched horns like the royal crown on its head, and said proudly: “Oh my God, how beautiful these horns are! They give me a prestige and beauty that no other animal in this forest possesses!”

Then he lowered his gaze and looked at the reflection of his legs. He felt very dissatisfied and said with a sigh: “But, look at these very thin and thin legs. They look weak, ugly and funny, and they do not fit at all with my great crown of horns! How I wish my legs were bigger and more beautiful!”

While he was immersed in his contemplation and evaluation of his body, he suddenly heard a terrifying sound interrupting the silence of the forest.

The roar of a hungry tiger coming towards him like an arrow!
The deer jumped up in terror and started running as fast as it could for its life.

Here, the skinny legs that the deer had despised moments before proved to be his greatest treasure; It was very light and fast like the wind, and carried it away from the tiger at breakneck speed across the open plains.

The deer was moving away little by little thanks to its strong, agile legs, and it almost escaped completely and entered the safety of the dense forest.

However, as soon as he entered among the tangled trees, his great and forked horns, which he was showing off, got stuck between the dense branches!
The deer tried with all its might to free itself, pulling and pulling its antlers, but they were stuck tightly like a trap.

The deer heard the sound of the tiger's steps approaching it quickly, and it could not escape because its camel horns tied it up.

In his last moments before the tiger pounced on him, the deer said with great sadness and remorse: “What a fool I am! You mocked my skinny legs, which almost saved my life, and boasted and took pride in my great horns, which became the cause of my ruin and death!”

Thus, this profound story teaches us that we often despise useful and practical things because we do not like their appearance, and we brag about false and beautiful things that may bring us harm and destruction. The true value of things lies in their usefulness and essence, not in their external appearance.
